exercise.name: Air Bike

reference.title: Air Bike (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Waist, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk flexion with rotation, alternating hip and knee flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as each elbow turns toward the opposite knee; breathe in as you pass through the middle. Breathe steadily, no breath-holding.

prescription.tempo: Slow pedalling, about 1-1.5 s per side; a short pause at each twist
prescription.progression: Slower pedalling, longer pause at each twist, straight leg lower to the floor

cues.text: Lie on your back, fingertips behind the head, elbows wide. Curl the head and shoulders up and lift both knees over the hips.
Breathe out: turn the right elbow toward the left knee as the right leg straightens away.
Switch: left elbow toward the right knee, left leg straightens.
Turn from the ribs, not by pulling the head; elbows stay wide.
Keep the low back down and pedal slowly.
Return to the middle, knees over the hips, and keep the shoulders up.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the head forward with the hands
mistakes.fix: Fingertips only, elbows wide; the turn comes from the ribs.
Slow down; turn the shoulder toward the knee and pause.

mistakes.mistake: Only the elbow moves (shoulder stays on the mat)
mistakes.fix: Lift and turn the whole shoulder blade off the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the leg straightens
mistakes.fix: Straighten the leg higher (about 45 degrees) until you can keep the back flat.

kinematics.norm: Head and shoulder blades off the mat throughout; lower back stays on the floor (ACE 2001 description)
Shoulder turns toward the opposite knee; elbow aims at the knee (ACE 2001); rotation amount is clinical opinion
Knee drawn toward the chest to meet the opposite elbow (clinical opinion)
Knees lifted to about 45 degrees and pedalled (ACE 2001); the straight leg hovers off the floor

sources.title: ACE-sponsored study, Francis and Davis (San Diego State University Biomechanics Lab) 2001, best and worst abdominal exercises, 30 adults, EMG relative to a crunch (ACE FitnessMatters, May/June 2001)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
Marshall and McGill 2010, the role of axial torque in disc herniation (Clin Biomech 25:6-9), porcine model

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The ACE result is from a magazine-published lab study (EMG relative to a crunch), not a peer-reviewed paper; treat the ranking as indicative.

Repeated loaded flexion combined with twisting promoted disc delamination in a porcine model (Marshall and McGill 2010); people with disc problems or flexion intolerance should pick a dead bug or side plank instead.
modify: Neck strain: rest the head in the hands without pulling, or cross the arms on the chest.
Low back arches: keep the straight leg higher.
Pregnancy or diastasis recti: avoid curl-up twists.
regressions: Feet on the floor, alternate elbow to opposite knee one side at a time.
progressions: Slower pedalling with a 2 s pause at each twist.
Straight leg lower toward the floor.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis keeps the shoulders curled off the mat the whole set. In the ACE-sponsored San Diego State study the bicycle maneuver gave the highest rectus abdominis activity of 13 exercises, about 2.5 times a standard crunch (Francis and Davis 2001).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Obliques turn the trunk so the elbow travels toward the opposite knee: the external oblique on the side of the moving elbow and the internal oblique on the knee side. Oblique activity was about 2.9 times a crunch, second only to the captain's chair (ACE 2001).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Obliques turn the trunk so the elbow travels toward the opposite knee: the external oblique on the side of the moving elbow and the internal oblique on the knee side. Oblique activity was about 2.9 times a crunch, second only to the captain's chair (ACE 2001).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas draws each knee toward the chest and holds the straight leg off the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas draws each knee toward the chest and holds the straight leg off the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the extending leg and help hold it up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the extending leg and help hold it up (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Right elbow turns toward the left knee
